### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-setting.object.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**15** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/tenancy-modes.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class), AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class), getPublicConfig (symbol, a method of class AuthManager))_
- `content/docs/plugins/index.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class), registerDeclaredDefault (symbol, a method of class SettingsService; a method of interface DeclaredDefaultHost; a method of interface SettingsReadSurface))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via AuthPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-setting.object.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7db865082df7d5a25cb11862aab382348adf4c02` — the merge of head `35da5d7b3efcf5a01262b9b854833e6c2796acb4` into base `4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7db865082df7d5a25cb11862aab382348adf4c02 && git checkout 7db865082df7d5a25cb11862aab382348adf4c02
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a 35da5d7b3efcf5a01262b9b854833e6c2796acb4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a && git merge --no-ff 35da5d7b3efcf5a01262b9b854833e6c2796acb4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3d64e99f21b8a80748cbe5e5fdae13b72c56e3a7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0007-settings-manifest-and-kv-store.md, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-declared-default.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-declared-defaults.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-live-status.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-live-status.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/settings-client.zod.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-setting.object.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-declared.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/settings/SettingsField.tsx, scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx, .changeset/auth-switches-read-declaration.md, .changeset/settings-declared-default.md, AGENTS.md
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

First record on this head. Faces: the governed rule text `docs/adr/0007-*` (the one `reviewFace` hit) and the declared narrowing. Read: card #38098 with triage 7232887955, claim 7233770569, claim note 7234902939 and dev report 7234889808; the PR body and its 15-file net diff against merge base `581ae76a`; the check-runs on the head. The tree was read in a detached worktree; nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the plugin-auth changeset: RIGHT. A reader of `GET /api/settings/auth` or `SettingsService.get('auth', …)` gets a different value for three keys with nothing stored, and a save that was accepted is now refused 400.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the service-settings changeset: RIGHT. `registerDeclaredDefault` and the type `SettingsDeclaredDefault` are added; a namespace with no provider resolves as before (`defaultOf` falls through to `reg.defaults.get(key)`).
- `Metadata-protocol: none` on both: RIGHT. No spec key, accepted value or manifest shape changes; a manifest author who registers no provider sees no change in what `default` does.
- `source: 'default'` kept for a declared value: RIGHT, without a spec shape change.
  - Every in-repo branch on the value reads it as "nothing stored and no `OS_*`", not as "equals the manifest default": about thirty sites in `packages/**` (`isExplicit` in `bindAuthSettings`, email, sms, storage, knowledge, organization locale and currency, membership policy) and two in the console (`SettingsField.tsx:349`, `firstRunChecklistLogic.ts:509`). None changes behaviour.
  - The console's "default: X" hint reads the chain's `default` entry (`SettingsField.tsx:228`), which `defaultOf` now answers, so the hint and the value agree. No console file reads `spec.default`.
  - The spec's own prose still says the old rung. See S2.
- `AuthManager.resolveDisableSignUp` public: RIGHT, named as a widening.
- The removed `declaredOffLabel` / `declaredOffText` copy: not a published surface. `auth-settings-live-status.ts` is not exported from the package index.
- One derived change is not named on either declaration line. See S1.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch and `@objectstack/service-settings` patch: RIGHT. With `Metadata-protocol: none` the level is `patch`, breaking or widening (AGENTS.md, changeset rule). Both packages sit in the fixed group.
- The narrowing owes, and the plugin-auth changeset carries: the `!` in the title, the **BREAKING** banner naming the affected reader, and one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The disposition fits: no stored row is read differently and nothing exists for `migrate meta` to rewrite. The category is refused only under `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, which this is not.
- No FROM/TO mapping is owed: nothing an author writes is removed or renamed.
- `Skills-docs: none`: RIGHT. No file under `skills/**` names the settings cascade, `SettingsService` or these switches.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-28T05:59Z: 53 runs, 30 success, 15 skipped, none failed, 8 still running (Test Core 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 of 10, and Type Check · workspace).
  - Success includes Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Docs and Type Check · source gates.
  - This record was read while CI was running. A closing read of the finished runs is owed before any landing step.
- The PR is a draft, `mergeable: true`, `blocked`.
- Tier: the PR is Tier H. `docs/adr/**` is governed, the ADR hunk replaces a line and rewrites the status line (not an add-only note), the diff carries package paths, and the body reads `Clause-②: yes`, so the low-risk arm does not apply. It lands only after an authorized APPROVED review by an account in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`. This record does not land it.
- Dev open question (keep the ADR amendment here or split it): the seat ruled A in 7234902939. Agreed: Prime Directive 13 asks for the amended status line with the behaviour change, and a split leaves the code contradicting the ADR until it lands.
- Claim surface: widened by claim note 7234902939 to the ADR and `config-resolution.mdx`. The diff stays inside it.
- Dogfood battery: reported at `3d64e99f`, this head, exit 0. The Dogfood Regression Gate check on this head is green.
- Dev out-of-scope finding, carrier none: the other `auth.*` keys with a deployment declaration (`password_min_length`, `password_max_length`, `membership_policy`, `mfa_required`, session and lockout windows, rate limits) still resolve the manifest default with nothing stored. Inferred, not measured. It needs a card; the seat files it.
- `Security-touching: yes`: the diff changes what the auth settings page reads, and which save of a sign-in method is refused.
- SQL push-down: nothing to report. The diff adds no read.

### ④ Design judgment

ADR-0007 amendment against its first consumer:
- The status line carries the amendment with date and card; rung 4 and a dated note under §Resolution state the same rule the code implements. Prime Directive 13 is met.
- The first consumer is in the diff (`auth-settings-declared-defaults.ts`), and `settings-service.ts` cites "ADR-0007 §Resolution, rung 4, as amended".

The seam (`settings-service.ts`):
- `reg.defaults` had three readers on base; all three now go through `defaultOf`: the cascade walk (line 2712), the cleared-key fallback in `validatePatch` (3627) and the `OS_*` coercion (1647). No other file in service-settings reads a manifest default for a registered key. Export, reset and `getMany` all pass through the cascade walk.
- The provider is asked on each use and nothing is cached. `undefined` and `null` fall through; a throw is said once per key at `warn` and the manifest default answers. A stored row and `OS_*` still win.
- `registerDeclaredDefault` refuses an unknown namespace or key; the map is separate from the manifest registry, so a manifest re-registration keeps the provider.

The three formulas against the running config (`auth-manager.ts`, read):
- `email_password_enabled`: `declared.emailAndPassword?.enabled !== false`, the expression `getPublicConfig()` uses.
- `signup_enabled`: `!resolveDisableSignUp(declared.disableSignUp)`. `getPublicConfig()` now calls the same method, which keeps the base expression: forced off under SSO-only or cloud-managed, then `OS_AUTH_SIGNUP_ENABLED` / `OS_DISABLE_SIGNUP`, then the declaration, then on.
- `require_email_verification`: `resolveEmailVerificationRequirement(posture in force, declared)`, the resolver `getPublicConfig()` and the wiring use.
- The formulas read the declaration captured in `init()`, not the running config. That is right: the bottom rung is also what a clear returns to and what the console shows as the default beside a stored value.
- The providers are synchronous and read no setting, so a read cannot recurse into the service.

The saves:
- Managed, declared off, nothing stored, save of `true`: now a change, reaches `signInMethodFloorPredicate`, refused 400 with `constraint: { cloudManaged: true, declaredEmailPassword: false }`. Pinned through `setMany` and the real `PUT`. Before, it stored a row that was not applied; the refusal is the honest answer. The settings pass still holds a row stored before the door.
- Self-hosted, declared off, nothing stored, save of `false`: no change, no predicate. Before, the floor judged it as turning off a method that was already off. The row is stored and applied, with the same value that runs.
- Self-hosted, declared off, save of `true`: a change; the floor passes it because email and password is on after it.

The banner:
- Nothing stored now agrees with what runs on both self-hosted and managed, so nothing is stated. A value stored on that a managed runtime holds off stays, as `warning`. Any other disagreement stays, as `warning`, so a failed registration or a thrown provider is still flagged.
- `declaredOff` copy: removed from all 11 locales; no reference is left in `packages/**`, `ui/**` or the cloud repo.

S1 (should-fix): open.
- On a deployment that declares `emailAndPassword.enabled: false` with nothing stored, `validatePatch` builds its value map from `get`, so `email_password_enabled` now reads `false` there. Ten `auth` keys are `visible` only while it is not `false` (`auth.manifest.ts`: `signup_enabled`, `require_email_verification`, `password_min_length`, `password_max_length`, `password_reject_breached`, `password_require_complexity`, `password_min_classes`, `password_history_count`, `password_expiry_days`, `mfa_required`). A hidden specifier is not validated, so a save of one of them is no longer judged for `required`, `options` or its bounds, where on base it was. Example: `password_min_length: 2` was refused (`min: 6`) and is now stored and applied.
- This is the behaviour a stored `false` already has, and saving `email_password_enabled: true` re-judges the gated keys (it is their `visible` dependency). It is a change to an accept set, and neither `Clause-②:` line names it.
- Fix: name it on the declaration line of the PR body and of the plugin-auth changeset. A test pinning it is welcome and not required.

S2 (should-fix): open.
- The published spec still states the old rung. `packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts:29` reads "4. manifest specifier.default", and the `SpecifierScope` comment at line 165 reads "falling back to `default` (declared on the specifier)". The generated page `content/docs/references/system/settings-manifest.mdx:26` repeats the first. `packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-setting.object.ts:28` reads "manifest specifier.default (source='default')".
- After this PR the ADR and `config-resolution.mdx` say one thing and the spec's own account says another. The seat's ruling was no spec shape change; these are comments, and no schema moves.
- Fix: amend the three comments to the ADR's wording and regenerate the reference page, in this PR.

Nits, none with an effect on correctness or the contract:
- N1 (open). `defaultOf` returns whatever the provider answers: no check against the specifier's type or options, and a provider that returns a promise would be served as the value.
- N2 (open). The `OS_*` coercion type follows the provider's answer, so a provider whose type differs from the manifest default changes how the same env string is read. The three auth keys are boolean on both sides.
- N3 (open). `SettingsDeclaredDefault` takes no context, so a later registrant cannot answer per organization. An optional argument can be added later without breaking.
- N4 (open). `differsText` says "the saved setting". Where the provider is missing or throws and nothing is stored, the banner is still raised and the sentence is then inexact.
- N5 (open). No case pins `signup_enabled` under `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED` or `OS_DISABLE_SIGNUP` (SSO-only is pinned and shares the formula), and the `validatePatch` clear and the `OS_*` coercion sites are covered only through `get`.
- N6 (open). A `signup_enabled` stored on under SSO-only or cloud-managed shows on while sign-up is forced off, with no statement. Unchanged by this PR; a follow-up card.

No must-fix. Two should-fix, S1 and S2, open on this head.

**VERDICT: PASS**

Delta record by the reviewer of record 7235028565 (PASS at `3d64e99f`, S1 and S2 open). The merge of `origin/main` brought no change to the PR's own hunks in `settings-service.ts`: `reg.defaults` still has one reader, `defaultOf`, and the same three call sites.

### ① Derived judgments

- Unchanged from 7235028565, with one addition: the hidden-key accept set is now named on the `Clause-②:` line of the PR body and of the plugin-auth changeset, under Widened, with the ten keys and the `password_min_length: 2` example. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

- No changeset for `@objectstack/spec` or `@objectstack/platform-objects`: accepted. Both edits are comments, both packages sit in the fixed release group, and Check Changeset passed on this head with no entry for them.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-28T07:24Z: 74 runs, 61 success, 12 skipped, none failed, 1 still running.
  - The one running is a second Check Changeset run, started 07:23Z by the PR body edit. The first Check Changeset run on this head finished green at 06:15Z.
  - Success includes all ten Test Core shards, Type Check · source gates (red on `35b33541` on the stale reference page), Type Check · workspace, Type Check UI, Dogfood Regression Gate and Governed Surface Queue Guard.

- Out-of-scope findings: the other `auth.*` keys and N6 are carried by #38184, open. N2, N3 and N4 are recorded in the PR body's Acceptance notes with no card.

### ④ Design judgment

Findings of record 7235028565, at this head:

S1 (should-fix): closed.
- Both declaration lines name the change. `auth-settings-live-status.test.ts` pins it: declared off with nothing stored, `password_min_length: 2` is stored; turning `email_password_enabled` on is then refused at `password_min_length`; the declared-on CONTROL refuses the same save.

S2 (should-fix): closed.
- `settings-manifest.zod.ts` rung 4 and the `SpecifierScope` comment, and `sys-setting.object.ts` rung 5, now read "what the running deployment declares for the key, else the manifest specifier.default". The regenerated `content/docs/references/system/settings-manifest.mdx` matches. No statement of the old rung is left under `packages/spec/src`, `packages/platform-objects/src` or `content/docs/references`.

The spec file as a schema-face hit: the two comment hunks agree with ADR-0007 rung 4 as amended and with `defaultOf`. Nothing else in the file changed.

The rework's code change, `defaultOf`: a provider that answers a thenable is now treated as a throw, said once, and the manifest default answers. It agrees with the type's amended comment ("Answered synchronously").

Nits, none with an effect on correctness or the contract:
- N1: closed.
- N2 (open, accepted). The `OS_*` coercion type follows the provider's answer; now pinned for a key with no manifest default.
- N3 (open, accepted). `SettingsDeclaredDefault` takes no context.
- N4 (open, accepted). `differsText` says "the saved setting" where the seam is missing or throws with nothing stored.
- N5: closed.
